newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Costello says rates set for growth, low CPI.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Costello says rates set for growth, low CPI.

text.p: Australian Treasurer Peter Costello said on Tuesday that monetary policy would not hold back economic growth if inflation targets were safe.
Costello, in a speech to an economists conference in Sydney which was issued here, also said that the inflation outlook was now better than forecast in the August budget for 1996/97.

"The (Reserve) Bank and the government take the view that monetary policy should not stand in the way of higher growth if the economy has the capacity to achieve that growth without threatening the low inflation objective," he said.

The improved inflation outlook had allowed the central bank to ease interest rates twice in recent months, he said, in late July and early November. The official cash rate was cut by 50 basis points each time to now stand at 6.5 percent.

"Recent developments confirm that price pressures are currently low and that underlying inflation is likely to remain comfortably below three percent over the next year," Costello told a economists' dinner.
"Information that has become available since the budget suggests that the inflation outlook is now even better than forecast in the budget," Costello said.

Annual underlying inflation was 2.4 percent in the September quarter, compared with the August budget forecast for a year-average rate of 2.75 percent in the year to June 1997, and comfortably within the central bank's 2-3 percent target.
The budget papers also forecast a headline inflation rate of 2.0 percent for the year compared with a 2.1 percent annual CPI rate in the September 1996 quarter.

The economy, as measured by Gross Domestic Product, grew 3.8 percent between the September quarters of 1995 and 1996, but the unemployment rate is creeping up, standing at a trend rate of 8.8 percent in October.
Costello also told the conference that he saw some signs of moderating wage rises, although the outlook remained risky.
"There have been some signs of a moderation in aggregate wage outcomes, with growth in average ordinary time earnings moderating significantly over the past year," he said.
"Nevertheless, risks to the wages outlook remain," he added, noting large current union claims. The government forecast five percent 1996/97 year-average wages growth.
Capacity utilisation was fairly high and the overall picture showed an economy with solid growth. Lower import prices, a result of the recent currency appreciation, had helped.

"Capacity utilisation remains relatively high albeit below the peaks of 1994," the treasurer said. "The housing finance data continue to be difficult to interpret but finance approvals for new dwellings appear to have troughed around mid-1996."
Costello said the employment forecast was achievable but reaching unemployment forecasts now seemed harder than at budget time.
Labor market data for the first three months of the year was consistent with the budget forecast for 1.5 percent year-average growth, Costello said.
"The sort of employment gains required to meet the budget forecast for the year as a whole are quite achievable and are consistent with the current level of job vacancies.
"The budget noted that unemployment would fall only gradually, as continuing employment growth encouraged more people to enter the labour force.
"Recent data on participation rates show how difficult this task will be, and the starting point for a fall in unemployment is now a little higher than anticipated at budget."
-- Canberra Bureau 61-6 273-2730
